verses.text: Now concerning spiritual things, brothers, I don’t want you to be ignorant.
You know that when you were heathen,  you were led away to those mute idols, however you might be led.
Therefore I make known to you that no man speaking by God’s Spirit says, “Jesus is accursed.” No one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” but by the Holy Spirit.
Now there are various kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit.
There are various kinds of service, and the same Lord.
There are various kinds of workings, but the same God, who works all things in all.
But to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the profit of all.
For to one is given through the Spirit the word of wisdom, and to another the word of knowledge, according to the same Spirit;
to another faith, by the same Spirit; and to another gifts of healings, by the same Spirit;
and to another workings of miracles; and to another prophecy; and to another discerning of spirits; to another different kinds of languages; and to another the interpretation of languages.
But the one and the same Spirit produces all of these, distributing to each one separately as he desires.
For as the body is one, and has many members, and all the members of the body, being many, are one body; so also is Christ.
For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether bond or free; and were all given to drink into one Spirit.
For the body is not one member, but many.
If the foot would say, “Because I’m not the hand, I’m not part of the body,” it is not therefore not part of the body.
If the ear would say, “Because I’m not the eye, I’m not part of the body,” it’s not therefore not part of the body.
If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would the smelling be?
But now God has set the members, each one of them, in the body, just as he desired.
If they were all one member, where would the body be?
But now they are many members, but one body.
The eye can’t tell the hand, “I have no need for you,” or again the head to the feet, “I have no need for you.”
No, much rather, those members of the body which seem to be weaker are necessary.
Those parts of the body which we think to be less honorable, on those we bestow more abundant honor; and our unpresentable parts have more abundant propriety;
whereas our presentable parts have no such need. But God composed the body together, giving more abundant honor to the inferior part,
that there should be no division in the body, but that the members should have the same care for one another.
When one member suffers, all the members suffer with it. Or when one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it.
Now you are the body of Christ, and members individually.
God has set some in the assembly: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracle workers, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, and various kinds of languages.
Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all miracle workers?
Do all have gifts of healings? Do all speak with various languages? Do all interpret?
But earnestly desire the best gifts. Moreover, I show a most excellent way to you.

footnotes.content: Paul doesn't scold them for confusion about the Spirit's gifts—he meets them where they are with gentleness. When we're tangled up about how God works in us, a wise teacher starts not with blame but with care.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He reminds them of their old worship—being pulled this way and that by voiceless idols, no choice of their own. It's the darkness before dawn: they know what deadness feels like, so now they can taste what it means to be led by a *living* Spirit who speaks.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The proof of the Spirit's work is always the same: *Jesus is Lord.* Not a fancy theology, not a gift that draws attention to itself, but a heart that names Jesus as the one who rules. Any spirit that points away from Him is not the Spirit of God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Look at that word *various*—God's gifts come in flavors and colors. And yet—one Spirit breathes through them all. Diversity is not disorder; it's the Spirit's signature.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Service takes many shapes in the church, but there's one Lord who calls them all. Whether you mend the broken or teach the young, it's the same Lord directing your hands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The same God holds it all together. Not many gods, not many powers—one God working all things through all people. When we forget this, we start competing with each other instead of joining His work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This changes everything: a gift isn't for showing off. When the Spirit moves through you, it's always for the good of *all*—the whole body. If you find yourself proud of what you can do, you've missed the whole point.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Wisdom and knowledge—they sound alike, but Paul knows they're different gifts. One is seeing deep into the mind of God; the other is knowing facts in their right order. Both come from the same Spirit and both are needed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Faith that moves mountains, healing hands—these aren't natural talents you can develop by trying hard. They're gifts the Spirit gives as He wills, not as we demand them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Miracles, prophecy, discerning spirits, tongues and their interpretation—Paul lists them matter-of-factly, as if to say: yes, these things happen in God's church. Not myths or exaggerations, but real workings of the Spirit, distributed among the body.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Spirit works all of these, *as he desires*—not as we desire. We don't negotiate with the Holy Ghost. We receive what He gives, grateful and humble, knowing He knows better than we do what the body needs in each season.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul reaches for the simplest, most beautiful picture: a body. One body, many parts, and here's the kicker—all of it *is* Christ. Not a metaphor he's just invented; it's the truth of who we are when we're joined to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Baptized into one body, Jew and Greek, slave and free—all the walls come down. One Spirit poured out on everyone. That should stop us cold. The divisions we carry are lighter than the unity He's already made.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A body isn't one part. If it were, it'd be a blob, not a living thing. The Lord designed us for multiplicity—different members, different work, all of it necessary.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A foot might mope: I'm not a hand, so I don't belong. But that's a lie the foot tells itself. It's *because* it's a foot that it belongs—the body needs feet, not duplicate hands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The ear says the same: I'm not an eye, so I'm worthless. And Paul says: no. An ear *is* an ear. That's your gift, your place. The body would be blind *and* deaf if all were eyes and none were ears.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If everything were an eye, you'd see the world but hear nothing, smell nothing, taste nothing. God knew what He was doing when He made us different. One sense alone is starvation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God arranged the members of the body *as He desired*. Not by accident, not by our voting or our preferences. The Master Architect knew the design He wanted, and He made you for a reason.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If everyone were the same part, where would the body *be*? It wouldn't exist. Sameness is dissolution, not unity. Only multiplicity makes a body.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul drives the point home: many members, but one body. The tension resolves not by everyone being alike, but by everyone belonging to the same Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The eye and hand—high honor in the ancient world—can't reject the others. Even (or especially) the strong parts of the body need the humble ones. Superiority is an illusion the Spirit shatters.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The weaker members are *necessary*. Not tolerated, not grudgingly included, but *necessary*. God's economy inverts ours. We hide what we think is weak; He honors it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The parts we're ashamed of, the parts we cover—we give them *more* honor, not less. A child knows to wrap a wound carefully. We protect what matters most because it's fragile, not because it's worthless.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God composed the body, deliberately giving extra care to what seems inferior. His hands arranged it that way. We don't get to rearrange what the Master has already built.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No division in the body—that's the aim. Members caring for each other with the same tenderness they'd show a wounded friend. When one part thrives, all flourish; when one suffers, all feel it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: This is the heartbeat of the church: mutual suffering and mutual joy. Not pity from above, not patronizing sympathy, but real *sharing* of the load. When your sister weeps, you weep; when she's lifted up, you celebrate with real gladness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You—all of you together—are the body of Christ. Not a building, not an institution, but a *body*—living, breathing, connected at the deepest level. And members individually: each one matters, each one is seen.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God has set them in order—apostles, prophets, teachers, workers of miracles. Not a hierarchy of worth, but an ordering of function. The body needs each kind, in season.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Paul asks the question everyone's thinking, and the answer is no. If everyone had the same gift, what would the church be? A body with all heads and no hands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret? No. And that's not a tragedy—that's wisdom. The Lord knew what He was doing when He scattered the gifts. None of us has everything; all of us have something.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Earnestly desire the best gifts—and then Paul pivots to show an even more excellent way. Readers today hear an echo in this: we chase spiritual prowess, gifts and victories, and the Spirit whispers: what you *really* need is love. It still stops us cold.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
